mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with lower S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as elevated interest rates compress equity valuations by increasing the discount rate for future cash flows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns show a positive correlation with FEDFUNDS (Rank IC > 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window, or the t-test for the mean return difference between high and low FEDFUNDS quintiles is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that reduces corporate borrowing and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.0% over any 3-year rolling window, or the mean return difference between FEDFUNDS>4.0% and FEDFUNDS<=4.0% is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0% and housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1300.0 thousand units, it signals a robust economic expansion that boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4.0% and HOUST > 1300.0 over any 3-year rolling window, or the mean return difference between the triggered and non-triggered periods is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), a federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.0% signals a restrictive monetary policy that reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS > 4.0% over any 3-year rolling window, or the mean return difference between the triggered and non-triggered periods is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong economic activity, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns show a negative correlation with INDPRO (Rank IC < -0.03) over any 3-year rolling window, or the t-test for the mean return difference between high and low INDPRO quintiles is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0%, it signals a tight labor market that supports wage growth and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4.0% over any 3-year rolling window, or the mean return difference between UNRATE<4.0% and UNRATE>=4.0% is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as rising inflation increases uncertainty and prompts investors to seek safe-haven assets.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns show a positive correlation with CPIAUCSL (Rank IC > 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window, or the t-test for the mean return difference between high and low CPIAUCSL quintiles is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of real GDP (GDPC1) indicates a strong economy, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns show a negative correlation with GDPC1 (Rank IC < -0.03) over any 3-year rolling window, or the t-test for the mean return difference between high and low GDPC1 quintiles is not significant (p>0.05).
